text:
alex: seeing a spike in OOMs on nightly e2e for large chat workloads. started after the FFN kernel switch to cuBLASLt fallback path.

maria: same. repro pretty reliably on g4dn-large run with batch=48, seq=4096, kv enabled. sometimes it comes up as fragmentation not raw capacity.

sam: quick snapshot from profiler: "peak_alloc = 42.1GB, fragmentation = 8.7GB, largest_free_block = 1.2GB". cuBLASLt workspace request jumps around due to block alignment.

lee: interesting — FlashAttention run had smaller working set but higher transient allocations. cuBLASLt does ephemeral workspace for matmul that our slab allocator isn't coalescing.

alex: attaching the minimal repro command:
```
./run_infer --model x-lr-34b --batch 48 --seq_len 4096 --kv-cache --kernel-policy=prefer_cublaslt
```

maria: stack trace shows allocation failures during FFN forward at tensor dgemm_workspace_alloc(). fallback to Triton reduces OOMs but latency regresses 12%.

sam: two ideas: 1) change slab freelist merging frequency, 2) introduce proactive compaction phase between requests when idle > 200ms.

lee: also we can bound cuBLASLt workspace via env var and force it to allocate in smaller chunks (it supports CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_MAX_BYTES). will trade perf for stability.

alex: can we tune workspace sizing heuristics: prefer smaller workspace for FFN if kv-hit-rate > 0.8 (so KV cache dominates memory) and use FlashAttention for attention-heavy requests?

maria: agree. propose heuristic matrix:
- if avg_seq_len>2048 && kv_cache enabled: max_ffn_workspace_frac = 0.12
- else if batch>32 and gpu_free<10GB: max_ffn_workspace_frac = 0.08
- default: max_ffn_workspace_frac = 0.2

sam: added a microprobe that simulates cuBLASLt workspace before kernel choice. it queries allocator.largest_contiguous() and compares to workspace need. if insufficient, force Flash/Triton fallback.

perf-bot: quick perf summary (dev run): baseline latency p95=210ms, cuBLASLt p95=190ms, safe-fallback p95=205ms, OOM rate baseline=0.01%, cuBLASLt=3.2%, safe-fallback=0.05%.

lee: that microprobe sounds good. need to avoid probing overhead. keep it as a fast best-effort check using cached largest_free_block per-stream.

alex: operational plan:
1) roll microprobe behind feature flag (ffn-ws-probe).
2) enforce env-controlled CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_MAX_BYTES default to 1.5GB.
3) slab allocator tweak: run freelist-merge every N=128 frees or on idle gap > 150ms.
4) telemetry: emit probe_decision, fallback_reason, largest_free_block, fragmentation_bytes.

maria: i'll open a PR with flags + perf tests. will include bench harness with batch seq sweeps and KV on/off.

sam: once PR is up I'll run nightly stress for 48h across GPU families (A100/RTX/GA100) and attach flamegraphs.

lee: tiny nit: ensure we respect alignment constraints for Triton kernels (64k alignment) when merging, otherwise we lose contig size.

alex: thanks. if we still see OOMs after compaction then next step is proactive KV-tail-eviction policy (drop oldest segments for very long context tails) + request-level hints for memory priority.

maria: 👍 will kick it off. tagging @oncall in case rollout triggers alerts.

perf-bot: alert-check: rollout flag enabled in canary - no alerts in first 30m."
